channel.title: The Dig — Error correction route
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Error correction route preset. Today's ranked reading list leads with 2611.22315, a connectivity-aware transpiler that selects routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis and reports 0.62x the two-qubit gates of Qiskit O3 across 55 benchmarks, and 2611.21270, whose Schmidt-time surrogate and QOC-guided search target pulse-level compilation latency under nearest-neighbor XY coupling; both are directly relevant to compiling for a small, sparsely connected spin-qubit QPU. The skim tier then covers 2611.21578 on temporally correlated leakage and cycle-dependent error accumulation for QEC benchmarking and mitigation, 2611.22260 on circuit-level geometry selection for rectangular surface codes under biased noise, 2611.23009 on dual-rail logical-physical boundary compilation with delayed realization binding, 2611.22166 on a common-clock superconducting qubit control scheme, and 2611.21397 on quantitative millikelvin microwave power measurement for cryogenic control-line calibration. No pay dirt today — 2 to skim.

item.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
item.description:
Skim new result — Timelike block suppression factor reaches μT=1.47±0.25 from patch sizes 3×3 to 7×7. Walking stability circuit suppresses temporally correlated |3⟩ leakage errors, reaching a logical error floor of ≤3.20×10−8 at 60 cycles.

Grade 0.524 · 3.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum error correction with silicon spin qubits”

Figure

Stability logical error probability versus syndrome extraction cycles on a 3×3 patch. The walking stability circuit bypasses the |3⟩ leakage-induced plateau of the standard circuit, lowering the error floor by two orders of magnitude to ≤3.20×10−8.

Asks

How do temporally correlated physical error mechanisms affect logical error suppression across space and time in surface code stability experiments?

But

Logical error floor at 60 cycles limited by ionizing radiation error bursts. Patch sizes 6×6 and 7×7 restricted to Z-basis only due to device layout constraints.

Tools

105-qubit Willow superconducting processor · surface code stability experiment · walking stability circuit · correlated matching decoder

Abstract

Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of 3 ×3 to 7 ×7, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of μ_T = 1.47 ±0.25, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state |3⟩. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model incorporating higher-state transport during syndrome extraction cycles. To suppress this error, we develop and realize a walking stability circuit, reaching a logical error probability floor of ≤3.20×10⁻⁸ at 60 cycles---two orders of magnitude below the standard construction---and limited by ionizing radiation error bursts. Finally, by adaptively terminating syndrome extraction based on decoder confidence in an offline analysis, we reduce spacetime logical error by 38% and time overhead by 34% compared to the optimal fixed-cycle strategy.

item.title: Logical error prediction and geometry selection for rectangular surface codes under biased circuit-level noise
item.description:
Skim new result — Response coefficients derived strictly from an unbiased reference circuit predict finite-bias circuit-level logical error rates with a median fold error of 1.09, cutting physical qubit counts by up to 42.4% (standard depolarizing) and 26.2% (superconducting-inspired) relative to square codes at physical error rate p=0.004 and target logical error rate PL,target=10−3.

Grade 0.565 · 4.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum error correction with silicon spin qubits” · Youshin Chung, Yujin Kang, Jun Heo

Figure

Physical qubit count as a function of idle noise bias for validated rectangular surface codes versus unrotated square code baselines at p=0.004 and PL,target=10−3.

Asks

Can the logical error response to a localized circuit-level bias be inferred from an unbiased reference circuit and transferred to finite-bias conditions without geometry- or bias-specific response fitting?

Before

Neglecting bias response gives a median fold error of 1.28, while mapping the full idle-channel change directly into the baseline parameter yields 3.18.

But

Unrotated rectangular surface codes only; evaluated at bias ratios η∈{1,2,3}, 0.003≤p≤0.008, and for memory experiments run over r=max⁡(L1,L2) rounds.

Tools

Stim and PyMatching · Score-function logical sensitivity estimation · Ordinary least-squares regression · Sinter Monte Carlo sampling

Abstract

Realistic quantum hardware often exhibits biased noise, but at the circuit level this bias may affect only a subset of operations and need not be transferred uniformly to logical errors. The logical response to a given physical bias is therefore central to selecting resource-efficient surface code geometries. Here, we study unrotated rectangular surface codes under standard depolarizing and superconducting-inspired circuit-level noise models. We first construct geometry-dependent logical error rate models from unbiased circuit-level simulations. We then use logical sensitivities to compare the responses to localized idle-bias and global physical error perturbations, defining logical-error-type-dependent response coefficients from an unbiased reference circuit without fitting to finite-bias data. These coefficients are incorporated through effective error parameters, yielding a median fold error of 1.09 over the evaluated finite-bias conditions. Geometries selected by the model are validated through direct biased circuit-level simulations. At a physical error rate of 0.004 and a target logical error rate of 10^{-3}, the validated rectangular codes reduce physical qubit overhead by up to 42.4% and 26.2% under the two noise models, respectively, relative to unrotated square codes. These results provide a practical link between circuit-level bias response and resource-efficient surface code design.
